body:
Were are you taking the expectation from that `--script` and `--editor` could be combined?

Given that `--script` is labeled a standalone tool in the docs I'd just expect an error.

Oh my bad, I thought these flags could be combined as it actually works just fine for my use case (other than these warnings when closing).

I use a launcher script extending SceneTree to be able to run my EditorScripts from the command line with the `--editor --script` flags combined when:
- access to the editor is needed from a script
- for convenience so I can run the same EditorScript from editor or command line.

This is a workaround for functionality discussed here: [Allow running headless editor scripts](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/discussions/8664)


One concrete use case is generating localization POT files from the command line. My script uses the editor's pot generation UI:
```gdscript
var localization := EditorInterface.get_base_control().find_child("*Localization*", true, false)
var file_dialog: EditorFileDialog = localization.get_child(5)
file_dialog.file_selected.emit(LOCALIZATION_PATH + "main.pot")
```
To be fair this is a janky workaround for the missing CLI option from this PR: #98422


So is combining `--editor` and `--script` unsupported? If so maybe it should produce an error instead of running - but it working is actually useful for workarounds like the one described above.
The warnings don't break anything for me. I just thought I would report them as they still happened with a minimal script when using the combined flags.
